claims.text: Her CXR chart: honeycombing, basal/peripheral reticulation (HRCT) → idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (UIP)
claims.quote: Honeycombing, basal/peripheral reticulation (HRCT) Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (UIP)

claims.text: Example HRCT: subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis (signet ring sign), with no findings inconsistent with IPF such as nodules; virtually diagnostic of IPF if clinical findings are compatible
claims.quote: Subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis (signet ring sign, where multiple thickened dilated bronchi are seen below a pulmonary artery) are present on high-resolution CT in a patient with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Findings inconsistent with IPF, such as nodules, are absent. These CT findings are virtually diagnostic of IPF if clinical findings are compatible.

claims.text: Buzzword: honeycomb lung on HRCT → idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (UIP)
claims.quote: Honeycomb lung HRCT Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (UIP)

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Diagnosis requires HRCT
HRCT: diffuse, patchy, subpleural, reticular opacities with irregularly thickened interlobular septa and intralobular lines; subpleural honeycombing; traction bronchiectasis
claims.quote: HRCT shows diffuse, patchy, subpleural, reticular opacities with irregularly thickened interlobular septa and intralobular lines; subpleural honeycombing; and traction bronchiectasis.

claims.text: Significant ground-glass opacities, nodules, or mosaic attenuation/air trapping suggest an alternative diagnosis
claims.quote: Significant ground-glass opacities, nodules, or mosaic attenuation/air trapping of the lung suggests an alternative diagnosis.

claims.text: CXR: typically diffuse reticular opacities in the lower and peripheral lung zones; honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis usually in more advanced cases
claims.quote: Chest radiograph typically shows diffuse reticular opacities in the lower and peripheral lung zones. Small cystic lesions (honeycombing) and dilated airways due to traction bronchiectasis are additional findings, usually occurring in more advanced cases with fibrosis.

claims.text: Causes IPF is identified histologically as usual interstitial pneumonia; affects men and women > 50 years in a 2:1 ratio; current or former smoking is most strongly associated
claims.quote: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, identified histologically as usual interstitial pneumonia, accounts for most cases of idiopathic interstitial pneumonia. Prevalence varies widely, in part due to regions with more rigorous screening, with some estimates as high as 495 per 100,000 annually in the United States (1). IPF affects men and women > 50 years in a ratio of 2:1, with a markedly increased incidence with each decade of age (2). Current or former cigarette smoking is most strongly associated with the disorder.

claims.text: UIP histology: subpleural fibrosis with fibroblast foci and dense scarring alternating with normal lung (heterogeneity); honeycombing occurs in all patients and increases with advanced disease
claims.quote: The key histologic findings include subpleural fibrosis with sites of fibroblast proliferation (fibroblast foci) and dense scarring, alternating with areas of normal lung parenchymal tissue (heterogeneity) (1). Scattered interstitial inflammation occurs with lymphocyte, plasma cell, and histiocyte infiltration. Cystic abnormality (honeycombing) occurs in all patients and increases with advanced disease.

claims.text: Symptoms Over months to years: progressively worsening exertional dyspnea and nonproductive cough; classic sign = fine, dry, inspiratory (Velcro) crackles at both bases; clubbing in about 50%
claims.quote: Symptoms and signs of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis typically develop over months to several years and include progressively worsening dyspnea on exertion and nonproductive cough, present in virtually every patient with IPF. Constitutional symptoms, such as low-grade fever and myalgias, are uncommon. The classic sign of IPF is fine, dry, inspiratory crackles (Velcro crackles) at both lung bases. Clubbing is present in about 50% of cases (1).

claims.text: Most patients deteriorate rapidly; median survival is about 3 to 5 years from diagnosis
claims.quote: Most patients deteriorate rapidly; median survival is about 3 to 5 years from diagnosis.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: antifibrotics (pirfenidone, nintedanib)
Pirfenidone and nintedanib slow progression; neither is shown superior; both require periodic liver function test monitoring
claims.quote: Pirfenidone and nintedanib are antifibrotic medications that slow progression of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (1, 2, 3, 4). There is insufficient evidence to support the efficacy of one agent over the other. The use of these agents requires periodic monitoring of liver function tests.
Supportive measures include oxygen and pulmonary rehabilitation.

claims.text: Otherwise healthy patients should be evaluated for lung transplantation at the time of diagnosis
claims.quote: Lung transplantation is successful for otherwise healthy patients with IPF. These patients should be evaluated for lung transplantation at the time of diagnosis.
